title: Last Night I Dreamed of Intercourse
text:
Last night I dreamed of intercourse, a realistic dream, hyperrealistic.

You martyr me with flesh

so that I will love you more

but not carnally.
editorial_note: The translation keeps Cardenal's frank diction and the turn from bodily desire toward non-carnal love.

title: They Told Me
text:
They told me you were in love with another man

and then I went to my room

and wrote this article against the Government

for which I am in prison.
editorial_note: The translation keeps the poem's sudden leap from private heartbreak to public punishment.

title: Girls Who Someday Will Read, Moved
text:
Girls who someday will read, moved,

these verses

and dream of a poet:

know that I made them for one like you

and that it was in vain.
editorial_note: The translation preserves the poem's address to future readers and its final deflation.

title: When the Golden Corteses Bloomed
text:
When the golden corteses bloomed

the two of us were in love.

The corteses still have flowers

and we are already two strangers.
editorial_note: The translation keeps 'corteses' as the flowering tree named in the original and contrasts its return with estrangement.

title: In the Hammock I Felt You Saying
text:
In the hammock I felt you saying

I did not choose you because you were holy

or made of the stuff of a future saint

I have had too many saints

I chose you for a change.
editorial_note: The translation keeps the hammock intimacy and the witty rejection of sainthood.
